audit.title: FunctionsRequest library API Reference
audit.contentType: developer documentation / API reference (auto-generated from Solidity NatSpec)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections lead with the signature, which is the right instinct for a reference. Weak spot: `REQUEST_DATA_VERSION` and `DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE` sections contain only a type declaration with no value and no one-line description — an empty liftable chunk.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Median 19-word sections, 10 tables, no section over 176 words, zero level skips — ideal RAG chunk boundaries.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Version strings present (`0.7.1`, `v1.3.0`, `v0.8`), but prose has only 2 numerals and the numeric constants show no actual values. "Only Remote secrets are supported" is a useful specific but buried in a table cell.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good primary-source link to the pinned `FunctionsRequest.sol` at `contracts-v1.3.0`, plus NPM package links. No link to the CBOR spec despite `encodeCBOR` being central.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Consumer contract developers use the FunctionsRequest library to build their requests" is a clean canonical opener. The `Location` enum table is highly quotable. Most function descriptions are single terse NatSpec lines.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, no og/twitter tags (measured). Headings are clean semantic HTML, which salvages the score. The page does reference `/llms.txt`, a positive site-level signal.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: All 16 fences are Solidity signature declarations — no imports, no usage example, no combined flow showing `initializeRequestForInlineJavaScript` → `addDONHostedSecrets` → `setArgs` → `encodeCBOR`. An agent cannot copy-paste anything executable.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the full API surface but only in "what is this signature" form. No "how do I build a request", no explanation of *when* `EmptySource`/`NoInlineSecrets` are thrown, no troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Consistent naming (`Request`, `Location`, `DON`), unambiguous prose. Terminology stable across sections.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured Solidity API reference for the `FunctionsRequest` library — every type, error, and function has a signature-first section with parameter tables, and the heading hierarchy is flawless (28 headings, 0 level skips, 10 tables). Its biggest GEO weakness is a combination of thin metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) and missing concrete values: the two constants that carry actual numbers (`REQUEST_DATA_VERSION`, `DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE`) show a type but no value, and no section shows a runnable end-to-end request build. The honest verdict: structurally exemplary, but it reads as a signature dump — a generative engine can cite the shape of the API but cannot synthesize *how to use it* or *when each error fires*.

recommendations.title: Fill in the missing constant values
recommendations.issue: Both sections show only `uint16 REQUEST_DATA_VERSION` / `uint256 DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE` with no value.
recommendations.change: Add the actual constant value and a one-line description, e.g. "`REQUEST_DATA_VERSION = 1` — the CBOR request-data schema version encoded into every request." Same for `DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE`.
recommendations.why: Quantitative constants are the single highest-lift specific; an empty declaration is an unliftable chunk that engines skip.

recommendations.title: Add a complete runnable request-build example
recommendations.where: After the intro line, before `## Types and Constants`
recommendations.issue: No section shows the functions used together; all fences are isolated signatures.
recommendations.change: Add one Solidity block with `import {FunctionsRequest} from "@chainlink/contracts/...";`, `using FunctionsRequest for FunctionsRequest.Request;`, then `req.initializeRequestForInlineJavaScript(source); req.setArgs(args); bytes memory data = req.encodeCBOR();`.
recommendations.why: Agents read reference docs to complete tasks; a self-contained, import-complete example is the most-cited artifact type and defends against parametric-prior guesses at usage.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings for the errors and common tasks
recommendations.where: `## Errors` section and a new FAQ block
recommendations.issue: Errors are listed as bare signatures — `error EmptySource()` — with no trigger condition.
recommendations.change: Under each error add "Reverts when …" (e.g. "`EmptySource` reverts when `source` is an empty string"). Add short H3s like "How do I add DON-hosted secrets to a request?" and "Why am I getting NoInlineSecrets?"
recommendations.why: Devs query by error string and "how do I"; concept-titled signatures lose retrieval that symptom-phrased headings win.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata (JSON-LD, canonical, dates)
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: "Solidity"`, and a `<link rel="canonical">`. Surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust; this is a site-template fix applicable across all API-reference pages.

recommendations.title: Promote the "Only Remote secrets are supported" constraint
recommendations.issue: Key constraint "\*Only Remote secrets are supported" is a footnote inside a table cell.
recommendations.change: State it as a standalone sentence under the `Request` struct: "As of v1.0.0, `secretsLocation` must be `Location.Remote`; `Inline` and `DONHosted` secrets are not supported at the struct level."
recommendations.why: A crisp canonical constraint prevents engines from hallucinating inline-secret support from generic priors.

recommendations.title: Add a CBOR spec citation
recommendations.issue: "Encodes a Request to CBOR encoded bytes" with no reference.
recommendations.why: Inline links to primary standards raise citation credibility on the page's most technical claim.

antiPatterns: Empty liftable chunks: two constant sections declare a type but no value or description.
Signature-only reference with zero usage code — an agent cannot execute anything without leaving the page.
Errors listed without trigger conditions ("see the function" implied but unstated).
offPageNotes: The page correctly references `/llms.txt`; ensure it is present and lists this URL — a site-level retrieval aid.
JSON-LD/canonical/date emission is almost certainly a docs-platform template concern; fixing it once propagates across every auto-generated API-reference page.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs — head metadata could not be verified here, so the metadata score reflects only what was served in-body.
